outlier.evidence: Ratings 6 (Reviewer_aPhY), 5 (Reviewer_HjX3), 6 (Reviewer_ZKdD) and 6 (Reviewer_xZYh). The spread is one point. The only 5 has confidence 2, and its author wrote 'I am fine with accepting this study if it is convincing enough to the other reviewers'.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 338-word review posted 2021-08-01, two weeks after the other three. It lists no weakness and calls the paper 'well ablated', while the other three A reviewers each asked for basic ablations. No discussion post. The AC's first sentence paraphrases its summary.

checkable_claims.claim: Transformer MD-Sine combines the same constant frequencies for both axes, so the encoding depends only on x1 + x2 and the baseline is useless.
checkable_claims.evidence: l.231-233 give no formula. The authors' reply gives sin(h*x1 + v*x2) with h and v 'just the default Transformer sinusoidal frequencies', so h = v, and they promised an ablation with different frequencies per axis. Fig. 3(b): MD-Sine ends near 3.68 bpd, worse than plain Sine-2D (about 3.64) in Fig. 3(a). The camera-ready drops the MD-Sine ablation.

checkable_claims.claim: Table 1, last column: the bold value is in the wrong row.
checkable_claims.evidence: SPICE bold is on Learnable-Fourier+MLP-2/2 (17.9), but Fixed-Fourier+MLP-2/2 has 18.4. The fixed variant also ties the learned 2/2 variant on BLEU-1 (46.1) and beats it on CIDEr (100.2 against 98.0), which weakens 'learnability is crucial' (l.243).

checkable_claims.claim: A baseline with a fixed (not learned) random W_r drawn from N(0, gamma^-2) is missing.
checkable_claims.evidence: l.239-242 and Fig. 3(d): 'Fourier' is fixed Gaussian features, with and without MLP. ZKdD conceded on 2021-08-22: 'you are right, thanks for pointing'.

checkable_claims.claim: The DETR experiments stop at 100k updates, before convergence.
checkable_claims.evidence: Fig. 4 caption: 'for the initial 100k steps'; AP there is about 0.27. In the authors' 2021-08-26 reply, after 300 epochs the proposal leads Sine-2D by 0.1 AP (40.2 against 40.1) and MLP by 0.2 AP. The authors: 'The difference between methods is small'.

checkable_claims.claim: In Fig. 3 most of the gain comes from the Fourier features and the learnable weights give no consistent gain; for DETR only AP and AP75 are shown.
checkable_claims.evidence: Fig. 3(d): Fourier, Fourier+MLP, Learnable Fourier and Learnable-Fourier+MLP overlap until about 85k steps and end within about 0.05 bpd. l.257: 'report validation bbox AP and AP75'.

checkable_claims.claim: The identity between Eq. 2 and Eq. 3 is wrong: r_x . r_y of concatenated cos and sin vectors gives cos(a)cos(b) || sin(a)sin(b), not a sum.
checkable_claims.evidence: An inner product of concatenated vectors sums over both blocks: sum cos(a)cos(b) + sum sin(a)sin(b) = sum cos(a - b), as l.158-159 state. The authors explained this, and aPhY did not raise it again.

checkable_claims.claim: Line 187 takes the L2 distance within one pair (x, y) instead of between two positions.
checkable_claims.evidence: l.185-186 define x and y as two objects with coordinates [x1, x2, x3, x4] and [y1, y2, y3, y4]; the sum of (xi - yi)^2 is the distance between the two objects.

checkable_claims.claim: The checklist claims code and a limitations discussion, but the paper has neither.
checkable_claims.evidence: Checklist 1(b) and 3(a) answer [Yes]. The paper has no limitations section and links only third-party codebases (footnotes 1 to 4). The authors conceded both.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_aPhY, 2021-09-02: 'I will increase my score from 5 to 6'; the review was edited that day. Reviewer_HjX3, 2021-08-14: 'I would not change my score'; 2021-09-02: 'the improvement is still slight'; the review was not edited. Reviewer_ZKdD replied once (2021-08-22) and did not edit the review. Reviewer_xZYh's edit (2021-08-02) predates the rebuttal (2021-08-10).
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: New experiments moved aPhY: MLP depth (3.62, 3.61 and 3.63 bpd for 1, 2 and 3 layers), Sine-4D+MLP (CIDEr 97.5 to 98.1, against 94.9 without MLP and 98.0 to 100.7 for the proposal) and DETR on held-out image sizes (39.5 AP against 38.9 for Sine-2D). aPhY still wrote that 'the same/nearby performance can be obtained with some other approaches'. HjX3 stayed at 5: the gains are 'still slight', and the held-out-size test may add a domain gap. No reviewer reacted to the converged DETR table (40.2 against 40.1 AP).

ac.evidence: Three 6s and a 5 whose author was 'fine with accepting'. The meta-review grants that the improvement is 'somewhat marginal' and accepts because the approach 'could be useful to the community'. Its first sentence paraphrases Reviewer_xZYh's summary ('outperforms the previous methods on a range of vision tasks'), and 'positional encoding has rarely been thoroughly studied' is xZYh's phrase. 'Useful to the community' echoes Reviewer_aPhY's last comment.

main_reasons_for_decision: No reviewer pressed for rejection: three 6s, and Reviewer_HjX3 (5, confidence 2) was 'fine with accepting'.
Rebuttal experiments moved Reviewer_aPhY from 5 to 6.
The AC judged the approach useful to the community despite 'somewhat marginal' gains.

outlier.evidence: 9 ('Top 15% of accepted NeurIPS papers') at confidence 5 after 3 hours, 2.6 points above the mean of the other five. 9tzP reviewed the paper at ICML as 'the grumpy reviewer' and now rewards the authors for fixing those objections: 'now you got me as a big supporter'. 9tzP calls the experiments 'very impressive'; the other five B reviewers question the size of the gains or ask for more experiments. Its one substantive inference, from the MD-Sine ablation, is wrong (see checkable claims). No discussion post.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 148 words. Says the method is verified on tasks 'including machine translation in NLP'; the paper has no such experiment. No discussion post.

8 ('clear accept') after 1.5 hours while calling the experiments 'the biggest issue of this work'. Kept 8 on 2021-09-03 ('I retain my score') although the relative PE comparison and the converged DETR results came only as promises.
Empty summary field and 2 hours. Claims that Eq. 2 splits into per-axis Fourier features, which Eq. 2 itself rules out. Raised to 6 with a six-word comment.

checkable_claims.claim: MD-Sine+MLP 'behaves so badly' that 'training the frequencies is crucial here'.
checkable_claims.evidence: MD-Sine uses the default Transformer frequencies on both axes (authors' reply in Committee A), so it encodes only x1 + x2 and ends worse than plain Sine-2D (Fig. 3(a), 3(b)). The paper's own fixed Gaussian features with MLP 'perform nicely' (l.241-242), and Fixed-Fourier+MLP-2/2 ties or beats Learnable-Fourier+MLP-2/2 on BLEU-1, CIDEr and SPICE (Table 1). The camera-ready drops MD-Sine.

checkable_claims.claim: The method is verified on tasks 'including machine translation in NLP'.
checkable_claims.evidence: Machine translation appears only in the Figure 1 heatmap of a standard Transformer (l.84-85). The experiments are ImageNet-64 generation, COCO detection and widget captioning.

checkable_claims.claim: Figures 3 and 4 give no precise numbers, and runtime is not reported.
checkable_claims.evidence: The submission has curves only and no runtime. The rebuttal gave 1.22 against 1.86 steps/s (Embed-2D) on Reformer, and 3.58 against 3.66 bpd. That 0.08 bpd gap is several times the gap at 100k steps in Fig. 3(a) (about 3.60 against 3.62); in Committee A the authors gave 3.6205 bpd at 100k steps for Learnable-Fourier with one MLP layer.

checkable_claims.claim: In Fig. 4 an MLP alone already beats the baselines, and learnable Fourier features add little.
checkable_claims.evidence: Authors' numbers at the end of Fig. 4: AP 27.5 (proposal), 27.0 (MLP), 26.5 (normalized Sine-2D, DETR's default). Fig. 4 shows the MLP and proposal curves close together.

checkable_claims.claim: Most of the improvement comes from the extra parameters that the MLP adds.
checkable_claims.evidence: Not for Reformer or widget captioning: l.215-217 size the Reformer variant to roughly match Embed-2D's parameters, and l.291-292 give 5.07M against Embed-4D's 5.11M. For DETR the paper gives no parameter counts, and the default Sine-2D has none, so there the concern stays open.

checkable_claims.claim: Eq. 2 is equivalent to learning Fourier features for each axis separately and concatenating them.
checkable_claims.evidence: Eq. 2 applies cos and sin to x W_r^T, and each row of W_r mixes all M coordinates. cos(a*x1 + b*x2) = cos(a*x1)cos(b*x2) - sin(a*x1)sin(b*x2) couples the axes; it is not a concatenation of per-axis features. The authors said so, and cSb4 rose to 6.

checkable_claims.claim: Object detection results cover only the first 100k steps; final performance is missing.
checkable_claims.evidence: Fig. 4 caption: 'for the initial 100k steps'. In B the authors only promised converged results; Committee A received them (40.2 against 40.1 AP).

checkable_claims.claim: Fig. 3 seems to show smoothed curves without error bars, and the broader-impact statement is dismissive.
checkable_claims.evidence: Faint raw traces sit behind the bold curves in all four panels of Fig. 3; checklist 3(c) answers [N/A] for error bars; l.341-342: the impacts 'are not applicable for this research'.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_cSb4, 2021-08-11: 'I increased my score to 6'; the review was edited that day. Reviewer_gVFH's review was edited 2021-08-29 with no comment, so the direction is unknown; the final rating is 5. Reviewer_TqtX, 2021-09-03: 'I retain my score'. Reviewer_9tzP, Reviewer_SAzJ and Reviewer_xpKV did not respond. After the rebuttal, reviewers posted 25 words in total.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: cSb4 moved after the ViT-B/16 ImageNet result (74.5% against 73.6% for Embed-1D, 90 epochs) and the correction on Eq. 2. gVFH got the same ViT number and the parameter counts and did not answer. TqtX kept 8 on argument and promises: relative PE 'will' be compared and DETR 'will' be trained to 300 epochs. B never saw the converged DETR results that A saw.

ac.evidence: The whole meta-review: 'The majority of reviewers agreed that this paper presents an interesting idea related to a relevant application.' Five of six reviewers are at 6 or above. It mentions neither the 9 nor Reviewer_gVFH's concerns, and it does not argue for a tier above poster.

main_reasons_for_decision: Three positive reviews (Reviewer_9tzP 9, Reviewer_TqtX 8, Reviewer_SAzJ 7) on the idea's simplicity and novelty.
Five of six reviewers at 6 or above; the AC cites 'the majority'.
The ImageNet rebuttal result moved Reviewer_cSb4 to 6; the one detractor (Reviewer_gVFH, 5) did not reply.

Unseen positions tested only on widget captioning, and 2685 of 2692 lie inside the training hull (Reviewer_ZKdD, Reviewer_aPhY, Reviewer_HjX3)

Table 1 SPICE bold on the wrong row; no-PE baseline; choice of gamma; KL loss (Reviewer_ZKdD)

Checklist claims code and limitations that are absent (Reviewer_aPhY)

No comparison with relative PE (Reviewer_TqtX); missing related work: LeViT, CPVT (Reviewer_gVFH) and learnable sinusoidal PE of Wang et al. (Reviewer_cSb4)

verdict: Both committees recommended a poster for the same reason. The method is a simple, new multi-dimensional generalization of sinusoidal positional encoding, with consistent but small gains, and an MLP alone gets much of them. Each committee had a single 5 and nothing lower, and neither 5 pressed for rejection after the rebuttal (Reviewer_HjX3 was 'fine with accepting'; Reviewer_gVFH did not reply). The gap in mean rating (A 5.75, B 6.83) comes from reviewer draw, not from a different reading of the paper. A's four reviewers all sat at the threshold, and two of them (Reviewer_ZKdD, Reviewer_aPhY, 12 hours each) pressed on the ablations. The rebuttal then showed a DETR gain of 0.1 AP at convergence. B drew three short positive reviews. Reviewer_9tzP (9, confidence 5, 3 hours) had reviewed the paper at ICML and rewards the authors for fixing that review's objections. 9tzP's inference that 'training the frequencies is crucial' rests on the MD-Sine baseline. In A, the authors said that this baseline uses the default Transformer frequencies on both axes, so it encodes only x1 + x2; the camera-ready drops it. Reviewer_TqtX gave 8 in 1.5 hours while calling the experiments 'the biggest issue'. B's other reviewers raised A's concerns. Neither AC added a reading of its own: A's meta-review paraphrases Reviewer_xZYh and calls the gains 'somewhat marginal'; B's is one sentence that cites 'the majority'. The same facts, weighed with different enthusiasm, gave different score levels and the same tier.
